claims.text: AlCoFeNi and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi are the magnetic high-entropy alloy systems under consideration.
AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi exhibits a hierarchically decomposed structure containing A2 precipitates in a B2 matrix.
Annealing at 600°C for 15 h in Ar followed by water quenching is the processing condition associated with the studied alloys.
The specified annealing and quenching treatment introduces the hierarchical B2 + A2 structure.
The A2 precipitates occur at multiple hierarchical size scales.
A2 gen-2 precipitates in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi contain three-dimensional magnetic vortex states.
Magnetic vortices within the A2 precipitates reverse successively during magnetization reversal.
The B2 matrix is weakly ferromagnetic.
Interactions between magnetic vortices in A2 precipitates and the B2 matrix create a complex magnetization process.
The hierarchical B2 + A2 structure increases coercive field through the proposed vortex-reversal and matrix-interaction mechanism.
AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi has a higher coercive field than AlCoFeNi under the reported measurements.
The reported coercivities are 9.56 mT for AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi and 1.45 mT for AlCoFeNi.
The baseline AlCoFeNi alloy lacks the hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure.
Interactions among the different magnetic elements remain unclear.
The effects of external magnetic field, stress, temperature, and strain on precipitate formation remain uncertain.
The hypothesis can be tested by measuring coercive fields and magnetization curves in alloys with and without the hierarchical structure.
Failure of AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi to show a significantly higher coercive field than AlCoFeNi would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is framed as introducing a microstructure, and the design proposes with-versus-without-structure controls, but the actual falsification rule compares two different compositions, AlCoFeNi and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi. This does not isolate the structural intervention from Cr-for-Co substitution and is not a composition-matched baseline.
